title: Local correction probability for linear functions
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $P$ be a Boolean-valued function on a set of $2^n+2^{n^2}$ indices, and let $	au:mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be the sign-valued function obtained from its first $2^n$ entries. Suppose the Boolean-valued function encoded by those entries differs from the linear function $x\mapsto\langle\gamma,x\rangle$ on at most a fraction $\delta$ of inputs, where $\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Then, for every coordinate $i$, the probability over uniform $y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ that $\tau(y)\tau(y+e_i)$ equals the sign encoding of the $i$th coordinate of $\gamma$ is at least $1-2\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean-valued proof function on $2^n+2^{n^2}$ indices
The encoded Boolean function is within relative Hamming distance $\delta$ of $x\mapsto\langle\gamma,x\rangle$
